nodes.description: DPP9 normally sits in a ternary complex with full-length NLRP1 and the autoproteolytically released NLRP1 C-terminal UPA-CARD fragment, sequestering that fragment so it cannot oligomerise. CARD8 is held by an analogous, though not identical, DPP9 complex - the CARD8 C-terminus does not engage the DPP9 active site the way NLRP1's does, and DPP9's catalytic activity rather than its binding is what restrains CARD8. Losing DPP9 removes both restraints at once, which is why one enzyme deficiency produces two tissue-specific arms of disease.
